topic: Never look directly at the sun (even during an eclipse) or welding light

youtube.title: Never look at the sun, even for a few seconds ☀️⚠️ #Shorts
youtube.description:
Never stare at the sun, not even during an eclipse.
சூரியனை நேராகப் பார்க்காதீர்கள், கிரகணத்தின் போதும் கூட!

• Your eye's lens focuses sunlight onto the retina, like a magnifying glass.
• The retina has no pain nerves, so you won't feel the damage happening.
• Ordinary sunglasses are not safe for viewing the sun or an eclipse. Use certified solar viewers or a pinhole projector.
• Welding light without a proper mask can burn the front of the eye, causing painful, gritty eyes hours later.
• Supervise children during eclipses and around welding work.
• See an eye specialist urgently if you notice blur, a dark spot or bent lines after looking at the sun.

gmb.text: Never look directly at the sun, even for a few seconds and even during an eclipse. The lens of the eye focuses sunlight onto the retina like a magnifying glass, and because the retina has no pain nerves, you will not feel the damage, which can be permanent. Ordinary sunglasses are not safe for looking at the sun; use certified eclipse viewers or a simple pinhole projector, and supervise children. Never watch welding light without a proper welding mask, as it can burn the front of the eye. If you notice blur, a dark spot or bent lines after looking at the sun, see an eye specialist urgently.
